headline: High-risk default data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s writable, networked Repl can expose secrets and collide with Opik’s broad egress/REST API surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between Opik and Replit Agent, so prompt injection is not default. However, Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and Opik can interact via REST API, so a manual file or API bridge could carry attacker-controlled text. The pathway is plausible but not inherent.
conditions: IF the operator copies Opik output into Replit workspace files or prompts Replit Agent with Opik-generated text, injection becomes possible.
IF a REST payload from Opik is treated as instructions by Replit Agent, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste model outputs into agent prompts without sanitizing.
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores embedded directives.
Use a human review step before any action-taking.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress; Opik also has broad network egress and REST API access. If they share a workspace or the same data is passed between them, sensitive code or secrets can be exfiltrated through either agent’s outbound calls. The blast radius includes secrets and deployment config, so this is dangerous by default once co-used.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are written into the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can read them and transmit them onward.
IF the operator places secrets in files or prompts accessible to Replit Agent, those secrets can leave via network egress.
IF both agents are used on the same project data, leakage can include source code and deployment configuration.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared files.
Restrict Replit Secrets access to the minimum needed.
Separate evaluation data from production code.
Disable outbound access for test runs where possible.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlists and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If both operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The Replit concurrency model explicitly persists shared filesystem state across sessions, making the conflict plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same Repl workspace or git checkout, write-write conflicts can occur.
IF Opik-driven automation and Replit Agent edits overlap in time, git history or files may be corrupted.
IF the operator relies on shared mutable state without locking, last-writer-wins behavior can lose work.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Commit or snapshot before handoffs.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Opik can generate or evaluate outputs through REST APIs, and Replit Agent can act on workspace files and shell commands. If Replit Agent consumes Opik output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. This is not proven as a default pipeline, but the interaction is plausible and the downstream impact can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF Opik output is fed into Replit Agent without verification, incorrect facts can be operationalized.
IF Replit Agent is allowed to execute shell commands based on upstream text, a bad recommendation can become a real change.
IF the operator uses Opik as a source of truth for code or deployment steps, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Cross-check Opik outputs against source files.
Use a validation script before applying changes.
Limit Replit Agent to read-only mode during analysis.
requires-engineering: add structured schemas and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Opik is an open-source observability/evaluation tool with broad network egress. If regulated data such as secrets or sensitive code is placed into the shared workflow, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or deployment configuration are stored in the Repl workspace, compliance obligations apply.
IF the operator routes EU personal data or PHI through either agent, residency and retention controls must be checked.
IF logs or traces from Opik retain sensitive prompts, retention policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts.
Review retention settings before use.
Keep secrets in approved secret stores only.
Document data flow and residency for the project.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal compliance review.
